title: Token throughput SLA validation harness for core realtime models
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a lightweight but robust tokens-per-second (TPS) validation harness that continuously verifies SLA compliance (latency/p95 and throughput) for our core realtime models in hosted and dedicated environments.

Background: We run periodic large-scale throughput suites, but we lack a fast-running, stable validation harness that can be used in CI, canary rollouts, and periodic health checks. Existing microbenches focus on steady-state token velocity but don't combine p95 tracking, KV-cache priming, and regression alerting in a single repeatable runner. This ticket scopes a pragmatic, test-first harness that integrates with our observability stack and regression detector.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Harness can run a 2–5 minute validation using synthetic and sampled real traffic profiles and report TPS and p95 latency per model variant.
- Integrates with metrics pipeline: emits metrics to metrics.redwood.com (tokens/s, p95_ms, error_rate) and creates a comparison against baseline for regression detection.
- Adds a lightweight dashboard and alert rule for >=10% TPS drop or >=20% p95 increase versus pinned baseline.
- CI job that runs on PRs targeting runtime kernels and model adaptors; run time <10 minutes.
- Canary gate: harness used automatically during canary rollout; failure blocks rollout.

Proposed approach / components:
1) Runner (go): small binary that can spawn N workers, control seq length distribution, and simulate prompt templates with optional prefix cache warmup. Supports: constant-token-rate, stepped-load, and poisson-arrival profiles.
2) Sampler profiles: curated set of 6 profiles (short-chat, long-context, streaming-incremental, embedding-batch, prefix-heavy, kv-cache-warmup). Profiles stored under infra/bench/profiles.
3) Calibrator: short calibration pass to set per-host concurrency to hit target TPS without queueing (measures tail-backpressure).
4) Metrics adapter: emit to Prometheus (pushgateway) and a JSON summary blob to S3 for regression jobs. Summary includes per-model: tokens_generated, avg_tps, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, error_count, retry_count.
5) Regression detector: small job comparing latest run to pinned baseline (branch/tag-based) and open a ticket or post to #perf-alerts when thresholds exceeded. Hook into existing regression alerting (ENG-9421 inspiration).
6) CI integration: GH action + Linear check that uploads artifacts and fails on critical regressions.

Instrumentation details:
- Use synthetic request bodies that match tokenization distribution; include a mode that replays sampled user prompts (scrubbed).
- KV-cache warmup should replicate cache occupancy policy (reuse common prefixes).
- Measure end-to-end server latency including RPC overhead and client batching semantics. Provide both server-only and end-to-end metrics.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- We intentionally keep the harness conservative: no very large sustained loads (avoid interfering with prod). Use rate-limits and tag test traffic.
- For dedicated clusters, harness will recommend but not automatically scale capacity; separate ticket for autoscale integration.

Open questions:
- Where do we pin baselines? Options: release-tagged S3 baselines, or per-branch ephemeral baseline. Proposal: pin to release baseline (release field) and allow PR-level ephemeral baselines for narrow tests.
- Alert thresholds: initial thresholds (10% TPS, 20% p95) are placeholders — propose evaluating over 2 weeks before locking.

Acceptance tests:
- Run harness against small model (test-model-v1) and verify metrics emitted to sandbox metrics and JSON summary in s3://redwood-bench-results/staging/ENG-90742/{}.
- Create PR that modifies kernel selection; ensure CI job runs and either passes or opens a regression alert.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/TPS+Validation+Harness (draft)
- GH proto repo (bench-runner): https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-runner/pull/48
- CI job example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-actions/blob/main/.github/workflows/tps-validate.yml
- Dashboard (work-in-progress): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/tps-validation?orgId=1

Longer-term follow-ups (separate tickets):
- Autoscale hook for Dedicated capacity based on calibration results.
- Extend regression detector to cluster-aware alerts and rollback automation.
- Add multi-model grouped runs (end-to-end workload tests).
